 Three bold-ish predictions for Warriors heading into 2026-27 NBA season 
 Dalton Johnson makes three bold-ish predictions for the Golden State Warriors heading into the 2026-27 NBA season. 
 By Dalton Johnson • 
 Published October 20, 2026 • 
 Updated on October 20, 2026 at 9:04 am 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg joins Kerith Burke on “Dubs Talk” and discusses his journey to the NBA ahead of Golden State’s 2026-27 NBA season. 
 When they go bold, we go bold-ish. As the saying goes … right? Right? 
 Everybody has grown tired of anybody picking three BOLD predictions for said team of said sport out of a hat. Here at NBC Sports Bay Area, we turn it up a notch. Or maybe it’s down a notch. Doesn’t really matter. 
 As someone who puts the ish in bold-ish, let’s first look back at my crystal ball that turned a bit too cloudy for me to see clearly going into last season. Remember, this is a process-based exercise where we’re allowed to laugh later at the results.

   SIGN UP HERE 
 First prediction: Steph Curry would set a career high in free throw attempts per game. 
 Laugh if you want, but Curry’s 5.1 free throw attempts per game were his highest in five seasons. It wasn’t a new career high, but it was tied for the fourth-highest of his career. 
 Second prediction: Buddy Hield would lead the Warriors in 3-point percentage. 
 No. Just no. Not at all. Go ahead and laugh. Hield made five threes in the season opener and then needed another seven games to reach that total. He shot a lowly 34.4 percent from three before being traded to the Atlanta Hawks last season, which was by far the lowest of his career.

 Third prediction: The Warriors would be a top-four team in the Western Conference 
 Stop your laughs and start your boos to kick me off the stage. The No. 4 seeded Los Angeles Lakers won 53 games. The No. 10 seeded Warriors won 37. So close!
 Now to gain your trust back, let’s get bold-ish with three Warriors predictions for the 2026-27 NBA season. 
 Rookie of the Year 
 Finalist. That’s the caveat.
 Yaxel Lendeborg has the chance to do something special in a stacked rookie class. Top draft picks AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson, Cam Boozer, Caleb Wilson and Darius Acuff Jr. are all hopefuls for the award with higher odds to win than Lendeborg. The Warriors’ No. 11 pick will match the play of many names taken higher than him, and pass a handful by season’s end.
 Chris Webber was the last Warrior to win the NBA’s Rookie of the Year, 33 years ago for the 1993-94 season. Webber started all 76 games he played and averaged 17.5 points, 9.1 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game. Will a rookie Lendeborg exceed those numbers more than three decades later? He has a case. 
 Lendeborg led the Warriors in points per game (15.6) and rebounds per game (7.4) in the preseason, while ranking second in assists per game (4.0) and shooting 56.9 percent from the field with a 43.8 3-point percentage. He did so averaging fewer than 24 minutes per game. 
 Steve Kerr has called Lendeborg his most pro-ready rookie he has ever coached, and it showed throughout the preseason, months after being the MVP of Las Vegas Summer League. Lendeborg was the Warriors' leading scorer in preseason and was given the veteran treatment of not even making the trip to Portland on the second night of a back-to-back for rest. 
 When Kerr and Curry both said Lendeborg needs to be more aggressive after their game in Hawaii, he reeled off games of 17 points, 23 points, 17 points and another 17 points. Lendeborg was the Warriors leading scorer in three games and their top rebounder three times too. He’s essentially playing the Jimmy Butler role as a rookie, and he’s most ready for it on this roster. 
 30 Ball 
 This isn’t a Curry section. It’s actually all about his backup point guard. 
 Fans had a field day when Brandin Podziemski scored 30 points at the end of last season against the Sacramento Kings. A social media account was even resurrected in what felt like one of the oddest holidays one could think of. No, this isn’t about him either. 
 The 30-burger fans will be celebrating is going to come from Brandon Williams. The newcomer has reached 30 points once through four NBA seasons. He’s about to make that twice, and maybe more. 
 Warriors players, coaches and fans saw Williams’ scoring burst on Christmas last season when he scored 26 points on 12 shot attempts. The Warriors’ front office clearly also had its eyes open to Williams as well, and he turned heads all through training camp and the preseason. Williams has what other Warriors don’t: Speed, shiftiness, a filthy handle and a penchant for getting to the rim. 
 Golden State’s third preseason game was a showcase of sorts for Williams as the main scoring threat, and he ran with his opportunity. Williams in 18 minutes scored 17 points on 7-of-11 shooting. The Warriors have 15 back-to-backs, and with the way they will be handling Curry’s health, Williams will have the ball in his hands enough for at least one 30-point game this season. 
 Trades Are Coming 
 The buzzword of media day and training camp is a clear theme of the entire season for the Warriors. They’ve pushed how they’re reimagining everything, and that’s multi-layered. It’s just a matter of how many layers get peeled by the Feb. 11 trade deadline. 
 Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy in the last two trade deadlines has acquired Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porziņģis in moves that sent out Andrew Wiggins, Jonathan Kuminga, Buddy Hield, Dennis Schröder, Kyle Anderson and Lindy Waters. The offseason was quiet for the most part. But Dunleavy has shown he’s always ready to make changes during the season, depending how it’s going. 
 He even traded for Schröder less than two full months into the season two years ago. We’re not saying Dunleavy will decide to deal that early, but there are many reasons to expect more activity this year.
 The Warriors have big expiring contracts in Butler ($56.8 million), Draymond Green ($27.7 million) and Porziņģis ($20 million, $3 million guaranteed next season). Al Horford is under contract for $6.8 million this season and has a $7.2 million player option for 2027-28, and De’Anthony Melton is making $6.1 million this season and has a $6.4 million player option for 2027-28. 
 However the Warriors are playing going into 2027, and through the end of January, will determine how this roster can look. The Warriors have their draft picks and they have moveable contracts. Dunleavy will get some kind of deal done in-season.
